result:
At 6:17 each evening, the window in the old bakery turns gold.

No one knows why. The sun has already slipped behind the rooftops, and the street is mostly shadow. But for three minutes, the glass glows as if someone inside has lit a small, private dawn.

People pause when they pass. A courier slows his bicycle. A child presses her mittened hand to the pane. Once, an old man stopped and smiled at his own reflection.

Then the light is gone, and the street becomes ordinary again.

But perhaps ordinary is only what we call the world between its brief acts of radiance.
